# Brivya

> Business-to-Agent infrastructure · v0.1.0-alpha.1

This website documents the open Brivya framework. It is not a callable production Business Agent. No business execution, OAuth or tool endpoint is advertised here. APIs are pre-stable. Discovery does not grant authorization.


---

# Documentation

Build a Business Agent, from its first contract to governed execution and platform integration.

Canonical: https://brivya.com/en/docs/
Version: 0.1.0-alpha.1
Language: en

## Start here

Brivya is open Business-to-Agent infrastructure. It models real business capabilities as typed contracts and connects REST, MCP and distribution ecosystems through one governed runtime.



New to Brivya? Start with the CLI, then explore the architecture and Restaurant reference. Existing TypeScript applications can begin with the SDK and protocol adapters.

## Developer journey

- [Quick Start](https://brivya.com/en/docs/quickstart/): generate and validate a business Manifest.
- [Architecture and safety](https://brivya.com/en/docs/architecture/): understand contracts, runtime and projections.
- [TypeScript SDK](https://brivya.com/en/docs/sdk/): use canonical types and execution.
- [Protocols and platforms](https://brivya.com/en/docs/adapters/): connect REST, MCP and reference distribution profiles.
- [Restaurant reference](https://brivya.com/en/docs/restaurant/): run the existing end-to-end contract tests.

## Current version

The public release is `0.1.0-alpha.1`. All 14 public npm packages use the `next` dist-tag. APIs are pre-stable. These docs describe the Alpha baseline, not a hosted service or a third-party publication guarantee.



[Explore versions and packages →](https://brivya.com/en/docs/releases/)

---

# Quick Start

Create your first business contract and validate the local development configuration.

Canonical: https://brivya.com/en/docs/quickstart/
Version: 0.1.0-alpha.1
Language: en

## Prerequisites

Use Node.js 20 or newer and npm. The local CLI flow does not require a cloud account, LLM API key or database.



```
node --version
npm --version
npm install -g @brivya/cli@0.1.0-alpha.1
```

## Create a business contract

```
mkdir my-business
cd my-business
brivya init
brivya validate
brivya inspect
brivya dev
```



`init` creates `business.agent.yaml`; `validate` checks the Manifest; `inspect` shows the resolved definition; `dev` validates and displays local configuration.



The generated Manifest is a contract scaffold. It is not connected to a real business system. CLI dev does not start an HTTP server or replace BusinessRuntime execution.

## Edit and observe

Maintain business identity, capabilities, protocols and security requirements in the generated Manifest. Inspect the scaffold before editing and keep validation in your workflow. To observe changes:



```
brivya dev business.agent.yaml --watch
```



You can pass an explicit Manifest path to validate, inspect and dev. Init does not silently overwrite existing files.

## Connect real capabilities

Use the SDK to register contracts, supply authorization and policy, implement Connectors and attach protocol adapters. Discovering a capability never grants permission to mutate business state.



Continue with the [SDK](https://brivya.com/en/docs/sdk/) or the [Restaurant reference](https://brivya.com/en/docs/restaurant/).

---

# Architecture and safety

One business truth, many projections. Every mutation follows the same governed execution path.

Canonical: https://brivya.com/en/docs/architecture/
Version: 0.1.0-alpha.1
Language: en

## Layers

AI platforms and Agent Hosts

↓

DistributionProfile · REST / MCP

↓

Canonical Business Agent · BusinessRuntime

↓

Connector · ERP / CRM / POS / Business APIs





Manifests, resources, capabilities and events define the canonical contract. Protocol adapters project invocation; distribution profiles project discovery, experience and packaging. Business authority stays in the contracts and runtime.

## Mutation path

```
Validate → Authorize → Policy → Approval when required
→ Idempotency → Connector → Transaction / Audit / Event
```



BusinessRuntime owns safety semantics. LLMs do not directly mutate business databases. Adapters cannot invoke Connectors to bypass authorization, policy or approval.

## Identity and authorization

- Agent Identity is not Authorization: recognizing a caller does not grant unrestricted execution.
- Discovery is not Authorization: a Manifest describes capabilities, not mutation permission.
- Platform Identity supplies context and still requires business authorization.
- UI Confirmation is not an ApprovalRecord: a client confirmation does not replace trusted evidence.



Protocol and experience projections must preserve risk, approval, permissions, idempotency and audit semantics.

## Core modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|  --- | --- |
| Core / Manifest | Typed contracts, parsing and validation |
| Policy / Runtime | Policy and governed execution |
| Experience / Distribution | Shared interaction semantics and projections |
| SDK / CLI | Developer APIs and local contract tools |
| Adapters / Connectors | Protocol entry points and business boundaries |

---

# TypeScript SDK

Reuse public business types, Manifest validation and the canonical runtime.

Canonical: https://brivya.com/en/docs/sdk/
Version: 0.1.0-alpha.1
Language: en

## Install

```
npm install @brivya/sdk@0.1.0-alpha.1
```



The SDK is a facade over Core, Manifest, Policy and Runtime. It does not introduce another authorization model or runtime truth.

## Load a Manifest

Read a Manifest generated by CLI init, then use canonical parsing and validation:



```
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { loadBusinessAgentManifest } from "@brivya/sdk";

const source = readFileSync("business.agent.yaml", "utf8");
const agent = loadBusinessAgentManifest(source);
console.log(agent.metadata.id);
```



Handle parsing and validation errors rather than executing with an invalid Manifest.

## Runtime and types

```
import {
  BusinessRuntime,
  CapabilityRegistry,
  runtime,
  type ActionRequest,
  type CapabilityContract,
  type Principal,
  type Delegation,
} from "@brivya/sdk";
```



BusinessRuntime and CapabilityRegistry reference the canonical implementations. Execution also needs capability registration, Connectors, trusted authorization context and runtime dependencies. Importing the SDK alone does not create a business service.

## Integration order

- Define capability inputs, outputs and safety requirements.
- Register contracts with CapabilityRegistry.
- Provide Connectors plus policy, approval, idempotency and audit implementations.
- Construct identity and delegation context on a trusted server.
- Execute through BusinessRuntime or adapters attached to that same runtime.



See the [Restaurant reference](https://brivya.com/en/docs/restaurant/) for execution tests and the [adapter guide](https://brivya.com/en/docs/adapters/) for protocol integration.

---

# Protocols and platforms

REST and MCP share the runtime. Distribution profiles reuse canonical business semantics.

Canonical: https://brivya.com/en/docs/adapters/
Version: 0.1.0-alpha.1
Language: en

## REST boundary

The REST adapter is an HTTP-framework-neutral execution projection:



```
POST /v0alpha1/capabilities/{capability}/execute

{
  "input": {},
  "preconditions": {}
}
```



Protocol metadata uses X-Brivya-Capability-Version, X-Request-Id, X-Correlation-Id, X-Causation-Id and Idempotency-Key headers. The body cannot assert trusted identity or approval state.



The hosting HTTP layer verifies authentication or session state and supplies a trusted RestSecurityContext. The adapter constructs an ActionRequest and calls BusinessRuntime.

## MCP projection

The capability `order.create@0.1.0` becomes the tool `brivya.order.create.v0.1.0`. Input and output JSON Schemas pass through to the MCP SDK.



The hosting transport/auth layer supplies a trusted McpContextResolver for verified identity, delegation, approvals and correlation metadata. Tool arguments are business input only. MCP annotations are hints, not authorization.



The default context contains only an untrusted Agent actor. Protected capabilities fail closed without a trusted resolver.

## WorkBuddy and WeChat AI

| Reference projection | Output |
|  --- | --- |
| WorkBuddy | connector-meta.json, mcp.json, skills/business/SKILL.md |
| WeChat AI | SKILL.md, mcp.json, runtime-bridge.json, components and registration patch |



These are reference generators and conformance baselines. Production publication still requires current official platform requirements, qualification and review. Third-party fields and APIs are not guaranteed stable.

## Before integration

- Preserve schemas, risk and permission requirements.
- Keep canonical approval requirements for high-risk actions.
- Preserve idempotency and audit across protocols.
- Never elevate client identity or UI confirmation into trusted authorization evidence.



SemanticExperience describes shared interactions; platform renderers provide native presentation while actions remain bound to canonical Capability IDs.

---

# Extension Host

Declare permissions explicitly and extend capabilities through a scoped Host API.

Canonical: https://brivya.com/en/docs/extensions/
Version: 0.1.0-alpha.1
Language: en

## Alpha baseline

The baseline includes Extension Manifest / Package, permission grants, expansion detection, install plans, Registry Client contracts, and worker / remote boundaries.



These framework contracts do not imply an existing hosted Registry or third-party marketplace.

## Effective permissions

```
Requested permissions ∩ Tenant policy ∩ Administrator grant
= Effective permissions
```



Declaring a permission does not grant it. A new version that expands privileges requires approval again. The host grants only the permitted intersection.

## Execution and secrets

```
Extension → Host API
→ Canonical Brivya Runtime / Governed platform service
```



The Host API enforces permissions. Secrets use opaque bindings rather than raw values. There is no raw secret-read Host API.

## Current limits

Phase 1 models worker and remote execution. WASM is deferred and arbitrary third-party in-process execution is outside the baseline. Validate host isolation, authorization and outbound policy before production use.



[Review runtime safety →](https://brivya.com/en/docs/architecture/)

---

# Restaurant reference

Follow discovery, reservations, orders and payment requests through deterministic contract tests.

Canonical: https://brivya.com/en/docs/restaurant/
Version: 0.1.0-alpha.1
Language: en

## Capabilities

| Capability | Business step |
|  --- | --- |
| menu.search | Search the menu |
| availability.check | Check availability |
| reservation.create | Create a reservation |
| order.create | Create an order |
| payment.request | Request payment |



REST and MCP use the same contracts and BusinessRuntime. The reference uses mock Connectors without an LLM provider or real payment SDK dependency.

## Get and run

```
git clone https://github.com/brivya/brivya.git
cd brivya
npm install --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
npm run ci
```



The current repository has no committed lockfile, so use the same npm install approach as CI. The root command builds, typechecks and tests, including the Restaurant RST-001..RST-024 contract matrix.

## Run reference tests only

```
npm run build
node --test examples/restaurant/dist/test/*.test.js
```



Build all workspaces first to prepare cross-package dependencies. Then run the compiled reference suite, covering execution, safety rejection and audit behavior with deterministic data.

## Reading path

- `examples/restaurant/src/manifest.ts`: business identity and capability declarations.
- `examples/restaurant/src/capabilities.ts`: capability definitions.
- `examples/restaurant/test/`: end-to-end evidence.
- `connectors/mock/`: mock business integration.



payment.request is a business payment request, not a connection to a real payment channel. The bootstrap URL is example identity, not a hosted live demo.

# Versions and packages

Understand the public Alpha modules, installation and stability boundaries.

Canonical: https://brivya.com/en/docs/releases/
Version: 0.1.0-alpha.1
Language: en

## v0.1.0-alpha.1

The first public Alpha was released on October 3, 2026. All 14 public npm packages use `0.1.0-alpha.1` under the `next` dist-tag. Pin versions explicitly while APIs remain pre-stable.



```
npm install @brivya/sdk@0.1.0-alpha.1
npm install -g @brivya/cli@0.1.0-alpha.1
```

## Public packages

- `@brivya/core`
- `@brivya/manifest`
- `@brivya/policy`
- `@brivya/runtime`
- `@brivya/experience`
- `@brivya/distribution`
- `@brivya/extensions`
- `@brivya/sdk`
- `@brivya/cli`
- `@brivya/adapter-rest`
- `@brivya/adapter-mcp`
- `@brivya/adapter-workbuddy`
- `@brivya/adapter-wechat-ai`
- `@brivya/connector-mock`

## Capabilities and limits

The baseline includes typed contracts, governed runtime, REST / MCP, reference distribution profiles, CLI / SDK, Restaurant E2E and Extension Host. The root workspace and Restaurant example are not published npm packages.



This version does not promise hosted Runtime, Registry, enterprise identity or automatic production platform publication. npm OIDC migration concerns release governance, not installation or website use.

## Before upgrading

- Review release notes for API and Manifest compatibility.
- Run business contract, permission, approval, idempotency and adapter tests.
- Keep canonical package versions aligned.
- Do not assume Alpha changes are stable compatibility guarantees.

# Contributing and security

Help improve business contracts, developer tools and platform conformance.

Canonical: https://brivya.com/en/docs/contributing/
Version: 0.1.0-alpha.1
Language: en

## Contributing

Contribute through issues and Pull Requests in the public implementation repository. Discuss substantial changes first. Preserve protocol and model neutrality, typed capabilities and explicit policy boundaries.


- Create a feature branch for a focused change.
- Add tests and public documentation for behavior changes.
- Run npm run ci and relevant release checks.
- Describe the problem, behavior, validation and compatibility in a PR.

## Security reports

Report potential vulnerabilities privately through the channels in SECURITY.md. Never post credentials, customer data or sensitive vulnerability details in public issues.



[Security reporting channels ↗](https://github.com/brivya/brivya/blob/main/SECURITY.md)

## License and brand

The public framework uses Apache-2.0. Brivya names and branding are governed separately by trademark policy. Framework use does not grant additional platform or brand permissions.



[Read the license ↗](https://github.com/brivya/brivya/blob/main/LICENSE)
